  1. net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api

Use a custom typeface

Choose a bundled, downloaded or resource-pack font and keep the same formatting codes, gradients and animations. Minecraft’s bitmap font is the default.

Choose a font in Mod Options

Open Mods → Chromatic Codes → Config → General → Typeface. Search for a family name or namespaced ID. Click a result to preview it, then choose Use typeface to return to the draft. The arrow keys move through results, Enter previews the highlighted result or accepts the current preview, and Escape closes the picker. The linked gallery uses the same draft for effect samples. Ctrl+Z undoes a font change, Cancel discards it, and Save & close applies it to text drawn through Minecraft’s FontRenderer.

The mod includes ten families, including Metamorphous, alongside the Minecraft bitmap option. To add more, place Font Pack 1.zip or Font Pack 2.zip in resourcepacks and enable it in Minecraft's Resource Packs menu. Font Pack 1 contains 100 families, including the ten in the mod. Font Pack 2 contains 100 additional families. Enabling both gives you 200 custom families. The supplied distance atlases cover ASCII and available Latin-1 glyphs. Other glyphs in the original font files use hinted rasterization.

  • Auto uses a grayscale, grid-fitted mask for small, nearly level text. It uses a distance field when the glyph is larger, rotated, sheared or appreciably stretched and the pack supplies that glyph’s atlas data.
  • Distance field prefers the pack’s pre-generated MSDF or MTSDF atlas for every covered glyph. An uncovered glyph or unavailable shader uses the raster path with the same layout.
  • Hinted raster draws grayscale masks at the needed physical size. This also works for packs with a font file alone.
  • Pack default follows the renderer specified by the selected family, usually Auto.

Auto measures the projected glyph axes in the active viewport, including GUI scale, local effects and whole-word transforms. Its default transition is 18 framebuffer pixels per em. A four-pixel band around the threshold keeps a repeated animated glyph on its current backend. Rotation and stretch have separate entry and exit points. The Transition control can change where that switch occurs. Logical advances, cursor positions and wrapping stay the same across backends.

Hinted raster uses grayscale coverage with quarter-pixel placement. It preserves each face’s design while grid-fitting stems to the framebuffer. Decorative letterforms with very thin strokes can still be difficult to read at tiny sizes. Increasing Size is an explicit layout change. Minecraft’s standard line spacing still applies in vanilla widgets, so reserve larger sizes for containers with enough room.

Drop a font download into your instance

Choose Open fonts folder in the Typeface picker to open config/chromatic_codes/fonts in your Minecraft instance. Drop in the ZIP and the open picker will update. A ZIP can contain nested folders, and you can also drop in loose TTF or OTF files. The picker groups faces using their family names and uses matching bold and italic files where available. It reads desktop outlines from the original download. WOFF, WOFF2 and font collections are skipped. These fonts use hinted rasterization because the download does not supply a distance atlas.

Choose which bundled fonts to show

Edit config/chromatic_codes_fonts.json. The open picker will update. Let bundledFontWhitelist be null to show all ten bundled fonts, or list the IDs to keep. For example, ["minecraft:vanilla", "chromatic_codes:metamorphous"] keeps Minecraft’s font and Metamorphous from the base mod.

Minecraft’s bitmap font is always available. The whitelist still lets downloaded fonts and families from enabled resource packs appear, including families a pack also supplies from the built-in set. If you hide a bundled font that you previously selected, rendering falls back to Minecraft’s font.

Add a TTF or OTF to a resource pack

Use a licensed outline font that you have permission to distribute. Place it under your pack namespace, for example assets/example/typefaces/book.ttf.

To make your family selectable, list it in assets/chromatic_codes/typefaces.json.

["example:book"]

Save the following descriptor as assets/example/typefaces/book.json.

{
  "regular": "example:typefaces/book.ttf"
}

The index is optional for families that a client addon registers explicitly. List each ID once per index. When two packs list the same ID, the picker shows it once and Minecraft uses its usual resource-pack priority to resolve the assets. Reload resources to pick up changes. An invalid descriptor, a fallback cycle, or an asset error in a resident family keeps the previous catalog active. Assets for other families are checked when used. The client log names the rejected resource.

Optional family fields
FieldWhat it controls
nameThe family name displayed in the picker. If omitted, the picker derives a name from the resource ID.
bold, italic, boldItalicProvide the matching outline files or face objects. When a variant is missing, the closest supplied face is used. The renderer uses real faces for bold and italic. Underline, strike and formatting reset still work.
fallbackAn ordered array of up to eight namespaced family IDs. A whole grapheme, such as a letter with a combining mark, uses the first face that covers it. Fallback faces use the main family’s em size and baseline.
size, baselineLogical em size and baseline below the line top, in GUI units. The defaults are 9 and 7. Both scale with the Size control.
mode, smallPixelsThe default backend and Auto threshold in physical pixels per em. Use AUTO, DISTANCE_FIELD or HINTED_RASTER. The threshold accepts integer values from 8 to 48.
hintingNATIVE uses FreeType’s light hinting with its normal hinter selection. AUTO forces FreeType’s automatic hinter when a font’s own hints give poor results. Both produce grayscale masks. If FreeType is unavailable, the client uses Java2D’s grayscale strike.

Missing glyph: Minecraft lets Minecraft draw and measure the entire string when none of the declared faces covers one of its clusters. Replacement uses the selected face’s missing-glyph mark and keeps the remaining text in that face. Minecraft also handles obfuscated text (§k). Unresolved family IDs use the bitmap path until the resource pack becomes available.

Supply sharper edges at larger sizes

For each face you want to render as a distance field, export a matching PNG and JSON from msdf-atlas-gen. Use glyph indices (-glyphset), as a shaped ligature or contextual form may have a different index from its Unicode input. Export the same font file and default font instance that the descriptor references. Include the glyph indices the face needs to draw, including shaped forms. Glyphs absent from the atlas still have the same logical placement and use hinted rasterization.

msdf-atlas-gen -font book.ttf -glyphset book-glyphs.txt -type mtsdf -size 48 -pxrange 6 -outerpxpadding 2 -format png -imageout book.png -json book-atlas.json
{
  "regular": {
    "file": "example:typefaces/book.ttf",
    "image": "example:typefaces/book.png",
    "metadata": "example:typefaces/book-atlas.json"
  },
  "smallPixels": 18
}

The PNG contains linear distance samples. Keep its channels intact. The renderer reads the median of the RGB distances and uses screen-space derivatives to antialias transformed edges. A true distance channel in MTSDF’s alpha can be present in the source asset. The shadow reads the same RGB glyph shape. Outline and extrusion use continuous coverage built from the vector outline, with the same logical thickness and reach at either foreground backend. Atlas filtering is bilinear, clamped to the page and limited to mip level zero. The exported boxes stay inside their own texel centers. Include outer padding when packing to protect the boxes from neighboring samples.

A range of 6 texels at 48 pixels per em is a starting point. The reader accepts symmetric distance ranges from 2 to 32 atlas texels, dimensions up to 2048 × 2048 and at most 16,384 indexed records per page. Vector outline width follows the configured radius. Extrusion sweeps the glyph over the configured reach, filling the gaps that would occur between separate offset copies of narrow strokes.

Measure and draw in a client GUI

Put these calls in client code. Use Typefaces to select a face while calling the usual Minecraft renderer. The selection scope is local to the client thread and restores the previous font when closed, even if a draw fails. Within it, measurement, drawing, wrapping, trimming and Minecraft’s text-field caret use the same shaping and spacing.

import net.minecraft.client.gui.FontRenderer;
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TypefaceSelection;
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.client.typeface.Typefaces;

public final class Recipe {
    public static TypefaceSelection book() {
        return TypefaceSelection.of("example:book");
    }

    public static void drawTitle(FontRenderer font, int center, int top) {
        var face = book();
        String title = "&[rainbow]Hello§r";

        try (var selection = Typefaces.with(face)) {
            float left = center - font.getStringWidth(title) / 2f;
            font.drawString(title, left, top, 0xFFFFFFFF, true);
        }
    }
}
import net.minecraft.client.gui.FontRenderer
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TypefaceSelection
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.client.typeface.withTypeface

fun book(): TypefaceSelection = TypefaceSelection.of("example:book")

fun drawTitle(font: FontRenderer, center: Int, top: Int) {
    val face = book()

    val title = "&[rainbow]Hello§r"
    face.withTypeface {
        val left = center - font.getStringWidth(title) / 2f
        font.drawString(title, left, top.toFloat(), -1, true)
    }
}
import net.minecraft.client.gui.FontRenderer
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TypefaceSelection
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.scaladsl.ClientTypeface

def book(): TypefaceSelection = TypefaceSelection.of("example:book")

def drawTitle(font: FontRenderer, center: Int, top: Int): Unit =
  val face = book()

  val title = "&[rainbow]Hello§r"
  ClientTypeface.withSelection(face) {
    val left = center.toFloat - font.getStringWidth(title) / 2f
    font.drawString(title, left, top.toFloat, -1, true)
  }
import net.minecraft.client.gui.FontRenderer
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TypefaceSelection
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.client.typeface.Typefaces

class TypefaceRecipe {
    static TypefaceSelection book() {
        TypefaceSelection.of('example:book')
    }

    static void drawTitle(FontRenderer font, int center, int top) {
        def face = book()
        String title = '&[rainbow]Hello§r'
        Typefaces.with(face).withCloseable {
            float left = center - font.getStringWidth(title) / 2f
            font.drawString(title, left, (float) top, -1, true)
        }
    }
}

CraftTweaker. Choose the font in the client’s General settings. Your script can use the same effect codes in an existing text field or tooltip. The client renders them when that widget uses Minecraft’s FontRenderer.

Add a styled line with <minecraft:diamond>.addTooltip("&[rainbow]Hello§r");.

For a single operation, Typefaces.measure and Typefaces.draw take the selection as an argument. To load a descriptor without an index, call Typefaces.register(ResourceLocation) after client resources are ready and keep the returned receipt in the client component that registered it. Close the receipt on the client thread when that component unloads. Closing an older receipt leaves a newer registration active. A family listed by a pack stays loaded regardless of API ownership.

If you set up a render callback, capture the immutable TypefaceSelection in that callback and open the selection scope inside each invocation. For a changing title, read the latest value on the client thread. Publish an immutable snapshot before sharing text from another thread. Remove the render callback before closing the registration it uses. Glyph effect callbacks still run at the original sampling points and on the threads described by the effect lifecycle.

Plan for reloads, Unicode and other renderers

The client indexes descriptors on resource reload. A preview or draw opens its chosen family and declared fallbacks. Search uses catalog names. The picker reads the regular outline for each visible name and caches its small row image as you scroll. The client keeps at most 16 recently used families within separate bounds for atlas pixels and outline bytes. Resource reload rechecks loaded faces and retains matching ones. An unread asset is checked the first time you select it. The Java 25 text shaper uses design advances, kerning, Unicode bidi levels and whole grapheme clusters. Formatting and fallback can break shaping at style or face boundaries. Color emoji, variable-axis selection and ligature-internal carets are outside this renderer’s layout. Tabs occupy four spaces. Fallback faces need a comparable design size and baseline for mixed text to look even.

Shaped strings and hinted masks use bounded caches. A first draw at an uncached strike can do a small rasterization and texture upload on the client thread. The client keeps up to four 1024 × 1024 mask pages and 4,096 mask keys per graphics context. Atlas assets are prepared outside the game. Reload releases replaced native faces and retires their textures when their owning context is current. A pack can be used with the Cleanroom client alone.

Formatting and animations apply to shaped clusters. Atlas padding never adds letter spacing, and atlas UVs stay attached to their glyph’s ink. Matrix uses the chosen face for its foreground, halo and code cells. When a face lacks a configured code symbol, the cell uses a supported symbol from the same face. Font-altering mods that replace Minecraft’s width or draw entry points can bypass these hooks. Custom fonts require a compatibility drawing context. If the distance shader fails, the renderer uses hinted raster and reports the shader diagnostic once for that context.
